title: Nilpotent coefficient extensions preserve a common higher direct-image bound
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, and $t\geq1$ an integer such that $I^t=0$. Use the categories $\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ of sheaves of modules over the constant coefficient sheaf on the small etale site, and similarly for $R/I$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Write $R^qf_*^R$ and $R^qf_*^{R/I}$ for the higher direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For every integer $N$, if $R^qf_*^{R/I}Q=0$ for every sheaf $Q$ of $R/I$-modules and every integer $q\geq0$ with $q>N$, then $R^qf_*^RM=0$ for every sheaf $M$ of $R$-modules and every integer $q\geq0$ with $q>N$. The same integer $N$ works independently of $t$; no finiteness or flatness of $M$ is required.

source.place: Tag 015B, label lemma-higher-derived-functors, part (1): the long exact sequence. The nilpotent-coefficient application is agent-written, extracting the coefficient-filtration argument in Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 6.5.11 and the former step 5 of the item; coefficient-change vanishing is the existing lem-sbc-coefficient-higher-direct-image-zero.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary $R$-module sheaf $M$. For $0\leq j\leq t$ define a subsheaf by $M_j(U)=\{s\in M(U):rs=0\text{ for every }r\in I^j\}$. This is a sheaf: restrictions preserve the displayed equations, and a compatible family glues in $M$ to a section satisfying each equation by uniqueness of gluing. It is an $R_X$-submodule because the coefficient ring is commutative. Since $I^{j+1}\subseteq I^j$, these subsheaves give $0=M_0\subseteq M_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq M_t=M$: $I^0=R$ contains $1$, and $I^t=0$. The category and its sectionwise kernels are those of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 03DA, label lemma-abelian: kernels and sheafified cokernels of module sheaves; elementary annihilator filtration constructed here.

proof.text: For $0\leq j<t$ take the cokernel $Q_j=M_{j+1}/M_j$ in the abelian category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so $0\to M_j\to M_{j+1}\to Q_j\to0$ is short exact. For $a\in I$ and $s\in M_{j+1}(U)$, every $r\in I^j$ satisfies $r(as)=(ra)s=0$, since $ra\in I^{j+1}$. Thus multiplication by $a$ on $M_{j+1}$ factors through $M_j$, and induces zero on its cokernel $Q_j$. Give $Q_j$ the $R/I$-action $\bar r\,x=rx$ on constants; independence of the lift follows because $I$ acts by zero. By the constant-sheaf construction [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and the sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], this action extends to $(R/I)_X$ (glue the action on sections of the constant presheaf); its module identities hold on constants and hence after sheafification. Its restriction along $R\to R/I$ is exactly the original $R_X$-action on $Q_j$.

source.place: Tag 03DA, label lemma-abelian: kernels and sheafified cokernels of module sheaves; elementary annihilator filtration constructed here.

proof.text: Fix $q\geq0$ with $q>N$. By the assumed bound, $R^qf_*^{R/I}Q_j=0$ for every $j<t$. Apply [lem-sbc-coefficient-higher-direct-image-zero] to the quotient ring homomorphism $R\to R/I$, the given qcqs morphism $f$, and the $R/I$-module sheaf $Q_j$ of step 2. It gives $R^qf_*^R Q_j=0$ for its restriction to $R$-coefficients, which step 2 identified with the cokernel used in the short exact sequence. This uses neither flatness of $R/I$ over $R$ nor preservation of injectives by restriction of scalars.

source.place: Tags 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree) and 0D6J (lemma-modules-abelian-unbounded), especially (3); coefficient-change vanishing is the cited existing DAG lemma.

proof.text: The category of $R_X$-module sheaves is abelian [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], and $f_*^R$ is additive and left exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] to each short exact sequence of step 2. Its exact sequence contains $R^qf_*^R M_j\to R^qf_*^R M_{j+1}\to R^qf_*^R Q_j$ for every $q\geq0$, including $q=0$ at the start of the sequence. When the outer two sheaves vanish, exactness forces the middle sheaf to vanish: its entire kernel is the image of a zero object, whereas its map to the zero object has kernel the whole object.

source.place: Tag 015B, label lemma-higher-derived-functors, parts (1) and (2), applied to complexes concentrated in degree zero.

proof.text: For the fixed $q$ of step 3, induct on $j$ from $0$ to $t$. The base is $R^qf_*^R M_0=R^qf_*^R0=0$, computed by the zero injective resolution in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. If $R^qf_*^R M_j=0$, step 3 gives $R^qf_*^R Q_j=0$, and the exact segment of step 4 gives $R^qf_*^R M_{j+1}=0$. Hence $M_t=M$ has $R^qf_*^RM=0$. Since $M$ and $q\geq0$, $q>N$, were arbitrary, this proves the claimed common bound. The induction uses only the same degree $q$, so it never enlarges $N$; it works also for $N<0$, when $q=0$ must be included, and uses no finiteness or flatness of $M$.

source.place: Tag 015B, label lemma-higher-derived-functors: elementary finite induction using the exact segments above.
